accuracy.evidence: Matches the Year 1 statutory requirement to read words with contractions such as I'm, I'll and we'll and understand that the apostrophe represents the omitted letters, and the Year 2 spelling requirement for apostrophes of omission. Every expansion was checked: can't from cannot drops n and o, it's is it is, we'll drops w and i, they're drops the a of are, don't drops the o of not.

misconceptions.evidence: Built around the errors teachers see in Year 1 and Year 2 writing: the mark placed between the two words (the do'nt prediction, ca'nt challenge option and gap feedback), no mark at all (Im option), keeping the dropped letter (I'am option and m8), confusing we'll with well (sorter cards and challenge), and reading the apostrophe as ownership (own tag). The adult notes warn against teaching it's and its with ownership rules too early.

lab_distinct.evidence: The flagcontr lab has the child knock individual letters out of two word tiles so the row closes up, then drag an apostrophe tile into the hole; unzip a short-form card onto its long form; drop the mark into one of several gaps in dont, shes and theyre; tap contractions in a running story; and pick two adjacent words in a sentence that merge. It shares no mechanic with the possession sorter and passed the shingle gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: The order goes from making to reading to placing to finding: first the child sees letters physically leave and the mark fill their space, then reads short forms back as long ones, then uses the missing letters to decide where the mark belongs, then finds contractions in connected text, then forms them inside a sentence. Each done line names the rule, for example that the mark goes exactly where letters were taken out.

predictions.evidence: Three committed guesses come before the evidence: what the little mark in I'm shows (tempting 'that I is a name', since I always has a capital), what can't means (tempting 'can it', which keeps the visible letters), and where the mark goes in dont (tempting do'nt, the gap between the two words). Each reveal compares the locked answer with what the tiles just showed.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each wrong challenge option has its own reply: well explains that well has no mark and we'll is we will, we all is corrected directly, own explains that nothing is owned in don't, end and between explain the mark sits in the gap left by the letters, Im and I'am each say what happens to the a, and none points to the word carrying the mark. A correct answer adds to a visible star streak.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with familiar words and the one new term, apostrophe, said in context; adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences to land inside the family target of grade 10 while still naming apostrophe of omission and the common partner words. Lab prompts stay under about ten words, and every short form is shown next to its long form after a success.

no_filler.evidence: The key idea gives the definition and three worked pairs in its first lines, the family tip is a concrete read-aloud habit with two questions, and the adult section covers the curriculum statements, exact terms, real mistakes and what each lab step does. Practice items each test one contraction fact rather than general reading chat, and numeric items count contractions or apostrophes in context.

mobile.evidence: Walked through on an iPhone 13 viewport and on desktop with all six steps, five tasks completed through Show me and the challenge shown. Letter tiles grow to 64 pixels on wide screens and wrap sensibly on a 360 pixel phone; the story chips wrap onto three rows with long forms printed under each found word, and a stale highlight on the joined sentence was fixed after the phone screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no violations in light or dark theme on either viewport. The canvas aria-label mirrors every spoken status, and each canvas action has a button twin: one per letter to knock out, a Put in the apostrophe button, the three long forms, one button per gap showing the word with the mark in place, and one per story or sentence word. Feedback uses a polite live region.
